findings.message: java.util.Random is used for verification code generation. This is cryptographically insecure. Additionally, the verification code is returned in the API response, lacks expiration, attempt limits, and rate limiting.

cve_candidates.title: Verification Code Security Weaknesses in mall-tiny
cve_candidates.cvss_note: PROVISIONAL - PR (Privileges Required) is marked X (to be confirmed). CVSS vector must be recalculated after dynamic testing.
cve_candidates.description: The verification-code mechanism uses java.util.Random, returns verification codes in API responses, and lacks expiration and attempt limits.
evidence: java.util.Random is used to generate 6-digit verification codes.
The generated verification code appears to be returned in the API response.
The verification code is stored in Redis.
No rate limiting logic found in generateAuthCode.
No attempt limit logic found in verifyAuthCode (implementation pending confirmation).
missing_evidence: Whether register, login, or password reset flows actually rely on verifyAuthCode.
Whether the affected code is present in a formal release tag.
Whether a dynamic PoC confirms the end-to-end impact.
Whether Redis TTL is set by default in RedisService.set().

duplicate_check.notes: Known mall-tiny CVEs (CVE-2024-57432 ~ CVE-2024-57435) cover different vulnerability classes (JWT hardcoded key, logout token persistence, default admin account, NPE DoS).

recommended_next_steps: Run local dynamic tests (curl, Redis checks).
Confirm affected version range via git tags.
Confirm verifyAuthCode implementation and call chain.
Privately report to the maintainer via GitHub Security Advisory.
